newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends higher on late demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends higher on late demand.

text.p: Late demand from some banks propelled Indian call money to 6.25-6.50 percent at close of trade on Tuesday against opening quotes of 5.5-5.75 percent, dealers said.
They said most of the day's business, done in the morning, was in the 5.25-5.5 percent range.
"But there was some last-minute covering (of positions) by a few banks," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "There were deals done at 6.5 percent at close."
Dealers said call money firmed up on Tuesday over Saturday's close of 2.75-3.25 percent on an outflow of funds from banks towards subscription to a repos auction held on February 8.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) accepted bids for 33.35 billion rupees at the February auction and successful bidders were required to make payment on Tuesday.
Dealers said the outflow of funds on this account more than offset an inflow of 14.8 billion rupees on account of repurchase of securities by the RBI.
Prices of government securities were steady to slightly lower in thin trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock traded on Tuesday 10 paise below its last traded price, dealers said.
The 13.40 percent 1999 stock traded at 101.60 rupees against last traded 101.62, they said.
Dealers said there were no trades in commercial paper or certificates of deposit.
